issues.legal_issue: An allottee has no enforceable vested right to possession of land where the proposed allotment would contravene legal restrictions or harm the public interest, and legitimate expectation or estoppel cannot compel an unlawful allotment.
material_facts: The administration included land in an industrial development scheme despite an existing forest reservation and restrictions on construction around an air-force base.
Applicants paid part or all of the price for plots, and some received lease deeds or formal possession, but the legal restrictions prevented the intended industrial use of some land.
The administration made a mistake in preparing the scheme, while the court found no material establishing mala fides.
issues.conclusion: The applicants could not compel delivery of the original plots or rely on vested rights, promissory estoppel, or legitimate expectation to require allotments contrary to law and public interest. The administration remained responsible for fair administrative redress, but monetary compensation was not ordered because it would also harm the public interest.
issues.legal_principle: Section 3(3) of the Capital of Punjab (Development and Regulation) Act, 1952, and Rules 4, 6 and 10 of the Chandigarh Lease Hold of Sites and Building Rules, 1973, do not create a vested right to use land contrary to other legal restrictions. Public interest prevails over promissory estoppel and legitimate expectation when fulfilment of a promise would breach the law. The Court relied on M/s Jit Ram Shiv Kumar v. State of Haryana, distinguishing Union of India v. Indo-Afgan Agencies Ltd. and Motilal Padampat Sugar Mills Co. v. State of U.P., and referred to M. Ramanatha Pillai v. State of Kerala and State of Kerala v. Gwalior Rayon Silk Manufacturing Co. It also applied the principles that public welfare is paramount and that the law does not compel the impossible, while recognizing the duty of administrative fairness to provide appropriate redress for losses caused by official error.

predicates.industrial_plot_allotment_proceeding: The proceeding concerns an allotment of land for industrial use.
predicates.proposed_land_legally_restricted: The proposed land is subject to a legal restriction that prevents the intended use.
predicates.proposed_use_harms_public_interest: Giving effect to the proposed allotment would harm the public interest.

issues.definition: When an industrial plot allotment concerns land legally restricted for the proposed use or would harm the public interest, the original allotment cannot be compelled.

issues.legal_issue: Giving priority to applicants who accepted smaller alternative plots over applicants who rejected them does not violate equality where the groups acted differently and suitable plots are scarce.
material_facts: Some applicants accepted the offer of smaller alternative plots, while others rejected it and challenged the offer and the forest reservation in court.
The challenges and stays delayed allotment of alternative plots, including to applicants who had accepted them.
The number of suitable smaller plots available in the existing industrial areas was limited.
issues.conclusion: The accepting applicants and the rejecting applicants were different classes, and the accepting applicants could be given priority for the limited available plots without violating Article 14. The rejecting applicants were not entitled to compete on equal terms for those plots.
issues.legal_principle: Article 14 permits differential treatment of applicants who form distinct classes on a just and reasonable basis. The Court treated the applicants’ different responses to the alternative offer and the limited availability of plots as a sufficient basis for priority to those who accepted the offer.

predicates.industrial_plot_allotment_proceeding: The proceeding concerns the allocation of alternative industrial plots to original allottees.
predicates.alternative_plots_are_scarce: The number of suitable alternative plots is insufficient to accommodate all applicants.
predicates.applicants_differed_in_accepting_smaller: Some applicants accepted the offer of smaller alternative plots while others rejected it.

issues.definition: When alternative plots are scarce and applicants differ in whether they accepted smaller plots, applicants who accepted them may receive priority.

issues.legal_issue: Applicants who accepted smaller alternative plots should not be charged a higher price for those plots when official error and delay deprived them of their original plots.
material_facts: Applicants accepted smaller alternative plots after the administration could not provide the originally allotted plots because of legal restrictions on the land.
The applicants had paid part or all of the original price, which remained with the administration.
The administration was primarily responsible for the mistake and delay, and the alternative plots were smaller.
issues.conclusion: The accepting applicants were to be charged the price prevailing at the time of their original allotment, with an adjustment or refund to account for the smaller plot.
issues.legal_principle: The rule of reasonableness and fairness binding on statutory authorities requires them not to increase the burden on applicants who were not at fault and whose payments remained with the administration. The authority must bear a portion of any loss caused by its own mistake.

rule.if: industrial_plot_allotment_proceeding and allottee_accepted_smaller_alternative and administration_caused_delay_or_error and original_payment_remained_with_administration

predicates.industrial_plot_allotment_proceeding: The proceeding concerns replacement plots for original industrial plot allottees.
predicates.allottee_accepted_smaller_alternative: The allottee accepted an alternative plot smaller than the original plot.
predicates.administration_caused_delay_or_error: The administration's mistake or delay prevented delivery of the original plot.
predicates.original_payment_remained_with_administr: The allottee's original payment remained with the administration.

issues.definition: An allottee who accepted a smaller replacement plot after administrative error or delay, while the original payment remained with the administration, is charged by reference to the original allotment price.

issues.legal_issue: Applicants who rejected smaller alternative plots may be offered suitable plots in a new industrial area at the price prevailing when the fresh allotment is made, subject to applicable eligibility requirements.
material_facts: Applicants who rejected smaller alternative plots were not entitled to priority alongside those who had accepted them for the limited plots in the existing industrial areas.
The administration had acquired and was developing land for a new industrial area outside the reserved forest area.

The administration proposed to consider the rejecting applicants for suitable plots in that area at the price prevailing on fresh allotment, subject to project viability and applicable industrial and environmental requirements.
issues.conclusion: The rejecting applicants were to be given an option to seek suitable plots in the new industrial area at the price prevailing on fresh allotment. Their previously paid price was to be credited against the new price if not already refunded. If they declined the option or their projects were not approvable, the original payment was to be refunded with interest.
issues.legal_principle: Administrative fairness required redress for applicants harmed by the administration’s error, but did not require giving them parity with applicants who had accepted the earlier alternative offer or charging the historic price for newly allotted land. Any fresh allotment remained subject to the Act, the Rules, applicable industrial policy, and environmental norms.

predicates.industrial_plot_allotment_proceeding: The proceeding concerns replacement industrial plots for original allottees.
predicates.allottee_rejected_smaller_alternative: The allottee did not accept the offer of a smaller alternative plot.
predicates.suitable_new_area_is_available: The administration has a new area in which suitable plots may be allotted.

issues.definition: When an allottee rejected a smaller alternative and a suitable new area is available, the allottee receives an option at the fresh allotment price or a refund if the allotment does not proceed.

issues.legal_issue: Applicants who were not parties before the High Court cannot join a later allocation process merely because they participated in subsequent negotiations or proceedings.
material_facts: Some original allottees did not participate as parties in the cases before the High Court.
Those applicants later sought to intervene, be impleaded, or obtain special leave, and some had been invited to participate in negotiations during the appeals.
The proposed alternative plots were limited, and substantial time had passed since the original allotments.
issues.conclusion: Relief was restricted to applicants who had been parties before the High Court; the remaining applicants’ intervention, impleadment, and special leave applications were rejected.
issues.legal_principle: On the facts, fairness and the applicants’ failure to pursue their claims earlier supported treating those claims as abandoned. Their later participation in negotiations did not create a cause of action or entitle them to compete for limited plots; speculative attempts to obtain an allotment were to be discouraged.

predicates.industrial_plot_allotment_proceeding: The proceeding concerns allocation of alternative industrial plots.
predicates.applicant_was_not_party_before_lower_cou: The applicant was not a party to the earlier court proceeding in which the dispute was heard.
predicates.applicant_later_seeks_to_join_allocation: The applicant later seeks to participate in the allocation through intervention, impleadment, or a further appeal.

issues.definition: An applicant who was not a party to the earlier proceeding and later seeks to join a limited allocation process is denied allocation relief.

issues.legal_issue: Limited available plots may be allocated by a fair draw among eligible applicants who accepted smaller alternatives and eligible applicants originally allotted plots of the same size as the proposed alternatives.
material_facts: The administration identified a limited number of vacant plots in the existing industrial areas.
It identified applicants who had accepted smaller alternatives and applicants originally allotted plots of one kanal, from whom no consent to a size reduction had been sought.
Eligibility depended on providing the required information and satisfying environmental norms, and some proposed industrial projects did not meet those norms.
issues.conclusion: The available plots were to be distributed by draw among the identified eligible applicants, with the administration deciding the procedure and being permitted to adjust plot sizes where necessary to accommodate eligible applicants. Eligible applicants not accommodated in those plots were to be considered for the new industrial area under the specified conditions.
issues.legal_principle: The Court balanced fair administrative redress against the limited supply of plots and required allotment to conform to eligibility criteria and environmental norms. Fresh allotments remained subject to the Act, the Rules, and the applicable environmental requirements.

rule.if: industrial_plot_allotment_proceeding and alternative_plots_are_scarce and applicant_is_eligible_under_current_requirements and (applicant_accepted_smaller_alternative or applicant_originally_sought_same_size_plot)

predicates.industrial_plot_allotment_proceeding: The proceeding concerns allocation of alternative industrial plots.
predicates.alternative_plots_are_scarce: The number of available plots is insufficient to accommodate every applicant.
predicates.applicant_is_eligible_under_current_requ: The applicant satisfies the applicable eligibility and environmental requirements.
predicates.applicant_accepted_smaller_alternative: The applicant accepted the offer of a smaller alternative plot.
predicates.applicant_originally_sought_same_size_pl: The applicant originally sought a plot of the size being offered and was not asked to consent to a reduction.

issues.definition: When plots are scarce, eligible applicants who accepted smaller alternatives or originally sought the offered size compete for available plots through a fair draw.

issues.legal_issue: An alternative plot within an area subject to a possible future security restriction may be allotted subject to cancellation if the restriction is reimposed, without liability for damages or interest on the refunded price.
material_facts: A restriction on construction around an air-force base had expired, but the administration reported that a similar restriction was under consideration.
Some alternative plots were within the area that could be subject to such a restriction.
The administration proposed conditional allotments and refund of the price if a later restriction required cancellation.
issues.conclusion: Allotments within the potentially restricted area could be made on the condition that they might be cancelled if the restriction was reimposed, with the price refunded but no damages, compensation, or interest payable by the administration.
issues.legal_principle: The Court permitted conditional allotments in light of the possibility of a future statutory restriction and the public interest in complying with it. The allottee’s price was to be returned if the restriction required cancellation, but the administration would not be liable for compensation or interest.

predicates.industrial_plot_allotment_proceeding: The proceeding concerns an alternative industrial plot allotment.
predicates.plot_is_in_area_at_risk_of_future_legal_: The plot lies in an area that may become subject to a legal restriction preventing its use.
predicates.allotment_is_made_subject_to_cancellatio: The allotment expressly permits cancellation if the restriction is imposed.

issues.definition: A plot in an area at risk of a future legal restriction may be conditionally allotted and, if cancellation follows, its price is refunded without compensation.

issues.legal_issue: A later industrial policy does not apply to earlier-phase allottees who succeed in a fresh draw held pursuant to the court’s directions.
material_facts: The administration had adopted a later industrial policy during the prolonged dispute.
The court directed a fresh draw for eligible allottees seeking plots in the existing industrial phases.
issues.conclusion: The later industrial policy was not to apply to allottees in the existing phases who succeeded in the fresh draw.
issues.legal_principle: The Court expressly confined the application of the later industrial policy by directing that it would not govern the specified fresh allotments in the existing phases.

predicates.industrial_plot_allotment_proceeding: The proceeding concerns the allotment of industrial plots.
predicates.fresh_draw_is_for_existing_phase_allotte: A fresh draw is held to allocate plots to allottees from an existing phase.

issues.definition: When a fresh draw allocates plots to allottees from an existing phase, the later industrial policy does not apply to those allotments.
